question.problem: A particle $P$ moves along the $x$-axis. When the displacement of $P$ from the origin is $x\,m,$ the velocity is $v\,m/s,$ and the acceleration is $4x\,{m/s}^{2}.$ If $P$ has velocity $2\sqrt{3}\,m/s$ when its displacement is $2\sqrt{2}\,m,$ find the values of $x$ for which $P$ is instantaneously at rest.
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14164351/assets/017463f3ac8abac9c2b00c4d9a715a4109a5f4bc1b070e0a12c4d3a7bac64351.png)

Since the acceleration of the particle $P$ is $4x\,{m/s}^{2},$ we have 

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=4x.
$$

Using the fact that

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}),
$$

we can rewrite our equation as

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})=4x.
$$

Integrating both sides of the above equation with respect to $x,$ we have

$$
\int \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})\text{d}x=\int 4x\,\text{d}x
$$

which gives the general solution

$$
\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}=2{x}^{2}+C.
$$

Now, since $v=2\sqrt{3}\,m/s$ when $x=2\sqrt{2}\,m,$ we can find the value of the constant $C,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2} & =2{x}^{2}+C \\ \frac{1}{2}(2\sqrt{3})^{2} & =2(2\sqrt{2})^{2}+C \\ C & =6-16 \\ C & =-10\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}=2{x}^{2}-10.
$$

Finally, the particle is instantaneously at rest when $v(x)=0\,m/s.$ We find the displacement of the particle when instantaneously at rest by substituting $v=0$ in the equation above and solving for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2} & =2{x}^{2}-10 \\ \frac{1}{2}(0)^{2} & =2{x}^{2}-10 \\ 2{x}^{2} & =10 \\ {x}^{2} & =5 \\ x & =\pm \sqrt{5}\,m\end{aligned}
$$
